scope: Theorem 4.1 (Bounded path estimate) of the manuscript “A Torsion-Free Group Algebra That Is Not Directly Finite” (preprints/A-Torsion-Free-Group-Algebra-That-Is-Not-Directly-Finite-October-4-2026/direct-finiteness.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 197 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 7950476863f21811), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 10-11. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is a constant ε > 0, depending only on the fixed alphabet and turn weights, with the following property. For every integer K0 ≥ 1, real number C ≥ 1, and integer I ≥ 0, the probability under PL that Γ contains a system satisfying all the following conditions tends to zero as n −→ ∞: 1. There are at most K0 positive-length paths. Each is closed and cyclically immersed, except possibly one immersed interval path whose initial vertex is xA or xB. 10 2. The total length satisfies L ≤ H ≤ CL. 3. There are at most I comparisons, satisfying (4.1), and b0 ≤ εH. In particular, ε is chosen before K0, C, I. The threshold in n and the rate of convergence may depend on these three bounds.
